# Flat geometry examples
#
# Each global vertex has one coordinate (t,x,y,z). The same coordinate is
# used in every 4-simplex containing that vertex. After the simplex list,
# enter one coordinate line for each global vertex in numerical order.

# Curved geometry examples
#
# Each 4-simplex has its own five local vertex coordinates. For every
# 4-simplex in the simplex list, the next five coordinate lines follow the
# vertex ordering of that simplex. The same global vertex may therefore have
# different local coordinates in different 4-simplices. Shared tetrahedra
# must still have the same intrinsic geometry.

# Curved Delta3 geometry from Phys. Rev. D 111, 024021 (2025)
# It is obtained by perturbing the boundary edge (2,6) of the flat geometry.
# Only the local coordinate of vertex 6 in the second 4-simplex changes.
# The following lists give five local coordinates for each 4-simplex.

# Delta3 curved geometry: local coordinates for each 4-simplex

[[1,2,3,4,5], [1,2,3,5,6], [1,3,4,5,6]]

# 4-simplex 1: [1,2,3,4,5]
0,0,0,0

0,0,-2.942830956382712,-2.942830956382712
